question.leadin: Answer the following about Douglas MacArthur.
question.text: Truman dismissed Douglas MacArthur and replaced him with Matthew Ridgway during this war. MacArthur led a surprise amphibious landing at Incheon (IN-chon) during this war.
question.clue: A commander on one side of this war proposed dropping 30 to 50 nuclear bombs on an opponent in order to create a radioactive wasteland and was criticized for rudeness to his country's leader at Wake Island.

swap.leadin: The half-brother of this country's leader was assassinated in the Kuala Lumpur airport in 2017.
swap.text: Name this country, led by the hereditary Kim family dictatorship. Its capital city, Pyongyang, is home to Juche (joo-chay) Tower, built by its first leader, Kim Il-Sung.
swap.answerHtml: North Korea [or the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea]
swap.clue: One leader threatened this country with "fire and fury like the world has never seen."

question.leadin: Answer the following about yellow ribbons in history.
question.text: Victims of the Sewol ferry disaster in this country are commemorated with yellow ribbons. The Miracle on the Han River refers to massive growth in this country's capital of Seoul.
question.answerHtml: South Korea [or the Republic of Korea; or ROK; prompt on Korea; reject “North Korea” or the “Democratic People’s Republic of Korea”]
question.clue: Nearly 300 high school students drowned on a ferry boat in this country in 2014.

swap.leadin: After conducting "literati purges" against members of the Sarim faction, one emperor banned an alphabet used in this peninsula to suppress criticism of his regime.
swap.text: Name this East Asian peninsula, once home to the kingdom of Joseon ["JOH-sun"]. This peninsula juts off of modern-day Russia and China and is separated from Japan by a namesake strait.
swap.clue: A military commander employed by a kingdom in this region designed so-called "turtle ships" to counter the forces of Toyotomi Hideyoshi; that commander was Yi Sun-Sin.

question.text: Yi fought for the independence of this longest Korean dynasty, which lasted from 1392 to 1897. The Hall of Worthies was a circle of scholars formed by this dynasty's emperor Sejong the Great, who personally created the Korean alphabet of Hangul.
question.clue: This dynasty was destabilized by succession crises called the Strifes of the Princes.

swap.leadin: According to the Samguk sagi, this kingdom was founded by Jumong, whose wife headed south to found the Baekje kingdom.
swap.text: Name this northernmost of the 3 kingdoms of the peninsula which now bears its name, along with Baekje and Silla. At its peak part of this kingdom extended into Manchuria and Siberia.
swap.clue: Some of the best-preserved art of this kingdom survives in the tomb of Dong Shou at a complex at Anak.

question.leadin: This kingdom ultimately broke up into the a group known as the Three Kingdoms, which included Baekje and Goguryeo.
question.text: This kingdom was ruled by the Gyeongju Kim clan for nearly 1000 years, making it one of the longest-surviving dynasties in history. Its aristocrats were called "sacred bone" or "true bone".
question.clue: Confucianism in Korea built upon earlier hierarchies such as the bone-rank system, which was used by this kingdom. This kingdom unified Korea in the 7th century after defeating its rivals Baekje and Goguryeo.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about numerically-named periods of Chinese history.
swap.text: Cao Cao, Sun Quan, and Liu Bei fought for control of China during this era between the Han and Jin Dynasties. It is the namesake of a novel by Luo Guanzhong.
swap.clue: The "Later" part of a period with this name was dominated by a Unified Silla that conquered Goguryeo.

question.leadin: The nickname for this policy supposedly came from a line in an Aesop fable titled for the "North Wind."
question.text: Name this policy instituted by Kim Dae-Jung. This policy attempted to de-escalate tensions between North and South Korea and eventually end North Korea's nuclear program.
question.answerHtml: Sunshine Policy [or Reconciliation and Cooperation Policy Towards the North; or Operational Policy Towards the North; or Embracing Policy]
question.clue: The adoption of this policy led to the joint operation of the Mount Gumgang Tourist Region and the Kaesong Industrial Park.

swap.text: China's civil service exam was imitated by the gwageo, an exam popular during this empire. Chogye Buddhism flourished in this kingdom, which was founded by Taejo and fought a series of wars against the Khitans.
swap.clue: Twenty-nine women from hojeok ("HO-juck") families were married to this dynasty's founder, Wang Geon ("gun").

question.text: In 1866, the American steamer General Sherman attempted to emulate Perry's expedition by visiting this non-Japanese East Asian city; however, the ship was destroyed by this city's residents. The USS Pueblo was captured off the coast of this capital city, and is still held in this city today.
question.clue: Nationalists deny that the Han Lelang ("luh-lahng") Commandery took this city from the Yan ("yen") general Wiman.

swap.leadin: This kinship system was weakened by the 1746 Dress act, which prohibited wearing kilts or identifying patterns.
swap.text: What name is given to these family and extended groups identified by their differing tartans?
swap.clue: What are these kinship groups in which members often took the chief's surname and which often have a distinctive tartan pattern?

question.leadin: These campaigns are sometimes called the "Ceramic Wars" because potters were kidnapped and moved to Arita, where they developed one country's porcelain industry.
question.text: Name these campaigns during which soldiers reportedly cut off the noses of their victims as trophies because heads were too unwieldy to haul around.
question.answerHtml: Japanese invasions of Korea [accept Hideyoshi’s invasions of Korea; accept Imjin Wars]
question.clue: That one of these events eventually ended at the Battle of Noryang.

swap.leadin: The sillok , the Veritable Records of this dynasty, stretch to 1,893 volumes.
swap.text: Name this dynasty, who built Five Grand Palaces in Seoul. This dynasty's fourth ruler was Sejong the Great, and it succeeded the Goryeo dynasty.
swap.answerHtml: Great Joseon [also accept Choson or Dyow syeon or Daejoseonguk or Taejosŏn'guk ]
swap.clue: This final dynastic kingdom of Korea that lasted from 1392 to 1897 when it was replaced by the Korean Empire. Sejong the Great established the Hall of Worthies in this kingdom.

question.text: In the initial phase of the war, North Korean forces pushed UN troops back to this feature, named for a very southern Korean city. The so-called "Bowling Alley" was one segment of this feature.

swap.leadin: It arose from a state founded by Hyokkose under its efficient military, the Hwarangdo.
swap.text: Name this dynasty which allied with Tang China to bolster its seventh to tenth century rule over Korea.
swap.clue: This dynasty employed a cultured class of cosmetic-using soldiers called the "flowering knights," or "hwarang."

question.text: The Unifed Silla employed this caste system to divide up the aristocracy using a measure of closeness to the throne. This system determined everything from the color of clothing worn to the maximum allowed size of the home.

swap.leadin: An inscription written on the Seven-Branched Sword describes how it was made by a crown prince of this kingdom.
swap.text: Name this kingdom whose last ruler, Uija ("ooh-EEH-jah"), was the progenitor of the Kudara no Konikishi clan. Yamato-era Japan lost 800 ships attempting to save this kingdom, whose incorporation into a larger kingdom was followed shortly by a similar conquest of Goguryeo ("GO-goo-r'yuh").
swap.clue: This kingdom absorbed all of the lands of the Mahan confederacy, thus seizing all of the present-day Jeolla ("jul-lah") region, under its great ruler Geunchogo ("geun-choh-goh").

question.leadin: This man's date with the bottom of the ocean in 1973 may have been averted through the quick action of ambassador Philip Habib, whom he later credited with helping to inspire his Nobel-winning Sunshine Policy.
question.text: Identify this politician who failed thrice in his bid for the Presidency when not enduring hunger strikes, house arrests, or exile, prior to becoming the first Jeolla native to achieve the office.
question.clue: Ambassador Philip Habib and Henry Kissinger supposedly intervened during an incident in which this man had weights tied to him and was almost drowned after he was kidnapped from a hotel in Tokyo.

swap.leadin: He declared his namesake "line" in a 1952 speech in order to protect his country's interests in the Sea of Japan, including fishing rights around the Liaodong Rocks. FTPE.
swap.text: Identify this man who died in exile in Hawaii, the first president of the Republic of South Korea.
swap.clue: Jimmie Leach observed his crackdown of the April 3rd uprising on Jeju Island.
